text:
mike: Hey team — customer in EU reporting missing audit events from last night's export to their SIEM. They see only policy events, but no token/grant events. File size looks normal though.

sam: Thanks @mike. Can you share the S3 object path + any request IDs or sample event ids?

mike: s3://redwood-audit-exports/customer-123/2026-03-16/part-0001.ndjson, object size 12MB. sample event id: evt_0a1b2c3d. They pull via a VPC proxy.

ingrid: Do we know whether the forwarder assumed the correct IAM role? If the exporter runs in customer VPC via proxy we might be dropping events during handshake with KMS.

juan: Checking export job logs now. I see repeated 403s from forwarder to export API: `403 Forbidden - KMS access denied` around 02:14 UTC.

sam: Could be our KMS key policy missing the `kms:Decrypt` for the exporter role. @juan paste the relevant log snippet.

juan: log snippet: ```[2026-03-16T02:14:05Z] forwarder=fw-82 request_id=req-9f8a KMSError: AccessDenied; KeyId: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123:key/abcd```

mike: Customer says they rotated their HSM in Jan, maybe key alias changed on their side.

ingrid: Two likely things: (1) VPC proxy may strip `x-amz-server-side-encryption` header on PUT which can cause our exporter to write unencrypted objects (we then filter those events downstream); (2) SIEM mapping filters out `event_type:token` if `kms_meta` is missing — schema-level exclusion.

eva: Quick repro plan: spin up a dummy forwarder behind a NAT/proxy; simulate KMS rotation; attempt export; confirm S3 object contents and whether indexer drops events. Steps: 1) assume exporter role; 2) POST to export API through proxy; 3) tail forwarder logs + S3 MD5 checks.

sam: Can you paste the curl the customer used? They ran: ```curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer x' -X POST https://export.redwood.com/v1/exports -d '{"range":"2026-03-16T00:00:00Z/2026-03-16T03:00:00Z"}' --proxy http://10.0.0.1:3128```

juan: When the proxy returns an intermittent error we retry but with truncated body. Found warnings: `WARNING: truncated body, expected 524288 but got 1200` in forwarder logs. That explains partial files.

mike: That aligns with customer report — partial content would drop token/grant events if those were near the end of the batch. How do we surface mitigation?

ingrid: Immediate mitigations: (A) ask customer to whitelist exporter endpoints and allow direct KMS calls from forwarder; (B) re-run export with `X-Force-Reexport: true` header so we generate a fresh file; (C) we should add exporter-side sanity checks to validate content-length/MD5 on upload and fail the job instead of accepting truncated uploads.

sam: I'll open a support ticket with the ask: re-export window, proxy whitelist steps, and sample repro instructions. Include the log snippets and recommend they check the KMS alias/role binding.

ops-bot: Created ticket #SUP-8421 (priority: high) — assigned to @sam.

eva: I'll prototype a small check: on upload-complete verify S3 object length and MD5 match the forwarder's computed value. If mismatch, mark job FAILED and alert infra.

mike: Customer confirmed they will try whitelist and re-run. Will update ticket when they do. thx :thumbsup:

sam: I'll follow up with a short KB note for customers using proxies + KMS rotations (include sample curl, proxy whitelist entries, and HSM/key alias checklist).
